It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}. {{nihongo|'''Hakui Shrine'''|羽咋神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Noto Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The current enshrined deities are the following four pillars:
; Principal deity
:* '''{{ill|Iwatsukiwake no Mikoto|Q11587884|qid=Q11587884|lt=Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto}}''' (いわつくわけのみこと)
:*: Also written "Iwatsukuwake-no-Mikoto" in some sources. The tenth {{ill|Imperial Prince|Q12886381|qid=Q12886381}} of the 11th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}. Regarded as the ancestor of the Hakui no Kimi.
; Associate deities
:* Iwakiwake-no-Mikoto (いわきわけのみこと)
:*: Son of Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto. Said to have been appointed Hakui no Kuni-no-Miyatsuko<ref>'Kokuzo Hongi' (volume 10 of the '{{ill|Kujiki|Q2716751|qid=Q2716751}}'), Hakui Kokuzo entry.</ref>.
:* Otokarihatatobe-no-Mikoto (おとかりはたとべのみこと)
:*: Consort of Emperor Suinin and mother of Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto.
:* Chigaeshi-no-Ōkami (ちがえしのおおかみ)
:*: Merged during the Meiji era.

== History ==
The founding date is unknown. {{ill|Iwatsukiwake no Mikoto|Q11587884|qid=Q11587884|lt=Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto}} was dispatched by order of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} when a monstrous bird appeared in this area tormenting the people. He slew the bird and promoted agriculture in the area. Later, the Hakui no Kimi clan, who governed the area, enshrined their ancestor Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto as their {{ill|Ujigami|de|Ujigami|es|Ujigami|fa|اوجی‌گامی|fr|Ujigami|ja|氏神|ko|씨신|mni|ꯎꯖꯤꯒꯃꯤ|pl|Ujigami|ro|Ujigami|simple|Ujigami|te|ఉజిగామి|uk|Удзіґамі|zh|氏神|qid=Q767655}}, which is said to be the shrine's origin.

In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}, completed in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed as "Hakui Shrine" in {{ill|Hakui District, Ishikawa|ceb|Hakui Gun|es|Distrito de Hakui (Ishikawa)|fa|شهرستان هاکوی، ایشیکاوا|fr|District de Hakui|id|Distrik Hakui, Ishikawa|it|Distretto di Hakui|ja|羽咋郡|ko|하쿠이군|pl|Powiat Hakui|uk|Повіт Хакуй|zh|羽咋郡|qid=Q1130953}}, {{ill|Noto Province|Q1047671|qid=Q1047671}}, and was ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

The Hachiman Shrine located about 200 meters to the southeast was the original site of Hakui Shrine (or alternatively, the site of Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto's residence). During the {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544}} era ({{ill|1469|Q6566|qid=Q6566}}–{{ill|1487|Q6652|qid=Q6652}}), shrine buildings were constructed atop the Ōtsuka kofun mound and the deity was transferred there. Another theory states that initially only a pine tree stood atop the Ōtsuka mound with no buildings constructed, and after the pine was destroyed by lightning during the {{ill|Hōreki|Q1194397|qid=Q1194397}} era ({{ill|1751|Q7615|qid=Q7615}}–{{ill|1764|Q7659|qid=Q7659}}), a treasure hall was built and made the main hall during the {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146}} era ({{ill|1804|Q6894|qid=Q6894}}–{{ill|1818|Q6964|qid=Q6964}}).

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}, and in Meiji 14 ({{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}}) it was elevated to {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}.

In Meiji 42 ({{ill|1909|Q2057|qid=Q2057}}), the deity Chigaeshi-no-Ōkami was transferred and merged from the Sanbyōkari Shrine atop the Hime-zuka (one of the Hakui Seven Mounds), which stood on the planned route of the {{ill|Nanao Line|Q5357471|qid=Q5357471}} railway. In {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 6 ({{ill|1917|Q2092|qid=Q2092}}), when the Ōtsuka was designated as a candidate imperial mausoleum, the shrine buildings were moved to the current location at the southern foot of the Ōtsuka's rear circular portion.

== Precinct ==
* Honden (main hall) — three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} with copper-plate roofing.
* Heiden
* Haiden (worship hall) — built in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 3 ({{ill|1832|Q7584|qid=Q7584}}), five-bay {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} with copper-plate roofing.
* Water of Goryō-yama — spring water from Mount Goryō.
* Ōtsuka (Goryō-yama) — one of the {{ill|Hakui-nanatsuka|Q11610061|qid=Q11610061}}. A {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}} designated by the Imperial Household Agency as the "Tomb of Iwatsukuwake-no-Mikoto." It remains behind the shrine buildings.
* Ōtani-zuka (Ōji-zuka, Kannon-zuka) — one of the Hakui Seven Mounds. A {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747}} designated by the Imperial Household Agency as the "Tomb of Iwaki-wake-no-Ō." It remains to the right of the shrine buildings.

== Auxiliary shrines ==
All are extra-precinct branch shrines located within Hakui City<ref>'Ishikawa-ken no Chimei,' Hakui Shrine entry.</ref>.
* Hachiman Shrine (Kawara-machi, {{ウィキ座標|36|53|45.75|N|136|46|56.48|E|region:JP-17_type:landmark|location|name=Hachiman Shrine (former main shrine)}})
*: Either the former shrine site or the site of Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto's residence. Originally located in front of {{ill|Hakui Station|Q5640629|qid=Q5640629}} but relocated to the current site in {{ill|1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754}} (Shōwa 35)<ref name="chunichi20230424">[https://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/677976 Enshrined deity to temporary residence — Hachiman Shrine in Hakui] Chūnichi Shimbun, accessed April 24, 2023.</ref>. As it was on the planned route of an urban planning road, in {{ill|2023|Q49622|qid=Q49622}} (Reiwa 5) the building was moved about 10 meters backward by hikiya (building-moving) construction; in April a temporary transfer ceremony was held, and in July a formal enshrinement ceremony returned the deity to the building<ref name="chunichi20230424" />.
* Sukunahikona Shrine (Kawara-machi)
*: Enshrined atop the Mizuinu-zuka (one of the Hakui Seven Mounds).
* Inari Shrine (Asahi-machi)
* Inari Shrine (Hon-machi)
* Uotori Shrine (うおとりじんじゃ, Shimade-machi)
* Kotohira Shrine (ことひらじんじゃ, Ōkawa-machi)

== Related sites ==
* Tsurugi-zuka ({{Coord|36|53|45.67|N|136|46|59.51|E|region:JP-17_type:landmark|name=Tsurugi-zuka (former site of Hachiman Shrine)}})
*: The former site of the extra-precinct Hachiman Shrine; said to be either the estate site of Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto or the original Hakui Shrine.

== Major festivals ==
* Kawawatashi Shinji (Saturday and Sunday in mid-September)
*: The mikoshi crosses the Chōja River to go to Hachiman Shrine. It is also said that Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto visits the female deity of Hachiman Shrine.
* Annual festival, Karadoyama Shinji Sumō ({{ill|September 25|Q2886|qid=Q2886}})
*: In honor of the enshrined deity Ishitsukuwake-no-Mikoto, who was said to love sumo, this event has been held since the {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} era ({{ill|1394|Q6398|qid=Q6398}}–{{ill|1428|Q6315|qid=Q6315}}). {{ill|September 25|Q2886|qid=Q2886}} is said to be the date of the deity's death.

== Cultural properties ==
== Ishikawa Prefecture designated cultural properties ==
* Intangible folk cultural property<ref name="list">[http://www2.city.hakui.ishikawa.jp/rekimin/index.php?action=pages_view_main&page_id=76 Cultural properties of Hakui City] (Hakui City Museum of History and Folklore).</ref>
** Karadoyama Shinji Sumō — designated as a Hakui City intangible folk cultural property on May 25, 2001 (Heisei 13). Redesignated as an Ishikawa Prefecture intangible folk cultural property on February 3, 2015 (Heisei 27) (city designation was rescinded).

== Hakui City designated cultural properties ==
* Natural monuments<ref name="list"/>
** Zelkova tree of Hakui Shrine — height 20.0 meters, estimated age 600 years. Designated January 11, 1972 (Shōwa 47).
** Sawara cypress of Hakui Shrine — height 21.0 meters, estimated age over 250 years. Designated January 11, 1972 (Shōwa 47).
